questions.stem: Arrange the following in correct chronological order. 1. Lucknow Pact between INC and Muslim League. 2. Champaran Satyagraha led by Gandhi. 3. Non-Cooperation Movement launched. 4. Jallianwala Bagh massacre.
questions.explanation: Lucknow Pact = Dec 1916. Champaran = 1917. Jallianwala Bagh = 13 April 1919. Non-Cooperation = Sep 1920 (Calcutta session) formally launched. Exam-favourite sequence because 1917-19-20 are tight.

questions.stem: Consider the following statements about the SIMON COMMISSION. 1. It was appointed in 1927 under the chairmanship of Sir John Simon. 2. All its seven members were British Members of Parliament. 3. It was opposed because it contained no Indian member. 4. Lala Lajpat Rai led protests in Lahore against it and was fatally injured in a police lathi-charge. Which of the statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: All correct. Simon Commission = 1927, 7 members all British MPs, 'all-white' hence Indian opposition, Lala Lajpat Rai died 17 Nov 1928 from injuries sustained in the Lahore lathi-charge led by J. A. Scott. His death was later avenged by Bhagat Singh, Rajguru, Sukhdev who killed J. P. Saunders (mistaking him for Scott).

questions.stem: Match List-I (movement / session) with List-II (year). A. Dandi March. B. Lahore Session of INC adopts Purna Swaraj. C. Gandhi-Irwin Pact. D. Quit India Movement launched. List-II: 1. 1929. 2. 1930. 3. 1931. 4. 1942.
questions.explanation: Dandi March began 12 March 1930. Lahore Session Dec 1929 (Purna Swaraj declared, flag unfurled at Ravi river midnight 31 Dec 1929). Gandhi-Irwin Pact signed 5 March 1931. Quit India launched 8 August 1942. Common confusion: Purna Swaraj year vs Dandi year — Lahore = 1929, Dandi = 1930.

questions.stem: ASSERTION (A): Gandhi withdrew the Non-Cooperation Movement in February 1922. REASON (R): The Chauri Chaura incident, in which a mob burnt 22 policemen alive, convinced Gandhi the movement had lost its non-violent character.

options.option_text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation
A is true, R is false
Both A and R are false

questions.explanation: Chauri Chaura incident 4 February 1922 in Gorakhpur district; Gandhi formally withdrew the movement on 12 Feb 1922. This decision deeply disillusioned the younger cadres (Motilal Nehru, C. R. Das) who later founded the Swaraj Party (1923) to contest legislative elections. Direct cause-effect; option A is textbook correct.

questions.stem: The CABINET MISSION (1946) proposed a plan for Indian independence. Which of the following was NOT a feature of its May 1946 plan?

options.option_text: A three-tier federal structure — Union, Groups of Provinces, Provinces
Immediate formation of an Interim Government
Partition of India into two separate sovereign dominions
A Constituent Assembly elected indirectly by Provincial Legislatures

questions.explanation: The Cabinet Mission Plan REJECTED partition and instead proposed a loose three-tier federation with grouping of provinces (A = Hindu-majority provinces, B = Muslim-majority NW, C = Bengal + Assam). Partition emerged later under the MOUNTBATTEN PLAN / 3 June 1947 Plan. Negative-stem exam trap — a legitimately hard distractor because partition is so strongly associated with 1947.

questions.stem: Consider the following acts and match with the key feature. List-I: A. Government of India Act, 1858. B. Indian Councils Act, 1861. C. Indian Councils Act, 1892. D. Government of India Act, 1909 (Morley-Minto). List-II: 1. Introduced separate electorates for Muslims. 2. Ended Company rule; India directly under the Crown. 3. First Indians associated with the Viceroy's legislative council via nomination. 4. Introduced the principle of election indirectly for legislative councils.
questions.explanation: Act 1858 — 'Act for the Better Government of India', ended Company, Crown's direct rule, created Secretary of State for India. 1861 Act — first nominated Indians in Viceroy's council (Banaras's Maharaja among them). 1892 Act — indirect elections introduced (bodies nominated members who elected to councils). 1909 Morley-Minto — famous for SEPARATE ELECTORATES for Muslims, often called the seed of partition.

questions.stem: During the Civil Disobedience Movement (1930-34), which of the following REGIONAL MOVEMENTS is INCORRECTLY matched with its leader?

options.option_text: No-Tax Campaign in Bardoli (earlier, 1928) — Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel
Salt Satyagraha in Malabar (Vaikom / Payyannur) — K. Kelappan
Forest Satyagraha in the Central Provinces / Maharashtra — Seth Govind Das, Veer Savarkar
No-Revenue / No-Rent Campaign in Uttar Pradesh — Jawaharlal Nehru

questions.explanation: Forest Satyagraha in Maharashtra / CP was led by figures like Mahadev Desai, and in specific pockets by local Congress leaders — NOT Seth Govind Das and V. D. Savarkar (Savarkar was not a Congress leader and had been interned). This is the INCORRECT pairing. The other three are textbook-correct.

questions.stem: Consider the following statements about the INDIAN NATIONAL ARMY (INA). 1. The first INA was organised by Capt. Mohan Singh in 1942 with Indian POWs of the Japanese. 2. Subhas Chandra Bose took over leadership of the INA in July 1943 at Singapore. 3. The INA's Rani Jhansi Regiment was an all-female combat unit. 4. The 1945-46 INA trials at the Red Fort were defended by, among others, Bhulabhai Desai and Jawaharlal Nehru. Which of the statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: All four are historically correct. Mohan Singh's 'first INA' was formed 1942 from POWs; it collapsed in a dispute with Japan and was revived under Rash Behari Bose, then handed to Subhas Bose in July 1943 (Singapore). The Rani Jhansi Regiment (founded October 1943) was led by Dr. Lakshmi Sahgal and was the first all-female combat regiment of its kind in Asia. The INA Red Fort Trials (Shah Nawaz Khan, P. K. Sahgal, Gurbaksh Singh Dhillon) were defended by Bhulabhai Desai, Tej Bahadur Sapru, Asaf Ali, K. N. Katju, Nehru and others.
